subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Direct Current: Steady and Constant
description: A micro-lesson that makes Direct Current: Steady and Constant usable.

hook.text: Batteries produce DC — current flows in one direction, always steady.

buildup.text: DC voltage holds constant over time. Plot it and you get a flat line.

discovery.text: Electronics love DC. Chips, LEDs, and sensors all need clean, steady voltage.

twist.text: DC is hard to transmit far. Voltage drops quickly over long wires.

climax.text: Edison championed DC power. He lost the war of currents — but DC rules electronics.

punchline.text: DC is simple, steady, and perfect for everything small.

quiz.question: Why is DC hard to transmit over long distances?
options: It can only travel through copper wire
Voltage drops quickly in long wires due to resistance losses
DC current reverses direction after a few kilometers
